For all ICAC investigations publicly reported more than 10 years ago, only a summary of the investigation is available online. To obtain the ICAC’s report or reports on these investigations, go to the relevant investigation summary below and click on the "Request the report" link.

2015

Rural Fire Service – allegations concerning catering supply and other matters (Operation Vika)

The ICAC investigated allegations concerning alleged corrupt payments related to the supply of catering and other products to the NSW Rural Fire Service (RFS) between 2009 and 2015. The Commission examined, amongst other matters, whether payments made by the RFS to catering companies controlled by one individual were induced by representations made by two RFS employees and, one RFS volunteer, and the company controller, which they knew to be false or misleading, or by those persons concealing facts from the RFS that they had a duty to disclose.

In its report on the investigation, made public on 17 December 2015, the Commission made findings of serious corrupt conduct against one RFS employee, the company controller and his mother.

The Commission also stated its opinion that consideration should be given to obtaining the advice of the Director of Public Prosecutions with respect to the prosecution of one RFS employee, the company controller and his mother for various offences.

The ICAC also makes four corruption prevention recommendations to the Rural Fire Service to help prevent the recurrence of the conduct exposed in this investigation in the future.

This report is no longer available online. Request the report.

University IT management – allegations concerning former IT manager (Operation Misto)

The ICAC investigated allegations that an information technology (IT) manager corruptly obtained benefits by issuing false invoices to the University of Newcastle, the University of Sydney and Macquarie University, when he held information technology (IT) management positions at each of the universities between 2005 and 2013.

In its report on the investigation, made public on 25 June 2015, the Commission made corrupt conduct findings against the IT manager, an IT consultancy company owner and a company director. The Commission also stated its opinion that consideration should be given to obtaining the advice of the Director of Public Prosecutions with respect to the prosecution of the university IT manager and the IT consultancy company owner for various offences.

The ICAC also made two corruption prevention recommendations to the University of Sydney and one recommendation to all of the universities to help prevent the recurrence of the conduct exposed in this investigation in the future.

This report is no longer available online. Request the report.

Ausgrid – allegations concerning former engineer (Operation Jarah)

The ICAC investigated allegations that a former Ausgrid engineer solicited and received benefits from Ausgrid contractors and subcontractors in exchange exercising his public official functions to show favour, or not to show disfavour, to them. It was also alleged that the Ausgrid engineer disclosed to contractors, and others, confidential information acquired in the course of his official functions.

In its report on the investigation, made public on 3 June 2015, the Commission made corrupt conduct findings against the Ausgrid engineer and six Ausgrid contractors. The Commission also stated its opinion that consideration should be given to obtaining the advice of the Director of Public Prosecutions (DPP) with respect to the prosecution of the Ausgrid engineer and five Ausgrid contractors for various offences.

The ICAC also made three corruption prevention recommendations to Ausgrid to help prevent the recurrence of the conduct exposed in this investigation in the future. 

This report is no longer available online. Request the report.

2014

University of New England - allegations concerning former chancellor (Operation Verdi)

The ICAC investigated allegations including that the former chancellor of the University of New England (UNE) provided confidential and/or sensitive information acquired in the course of their official functions as chancellor, in connection with the sale of the Services UNE Limited-owned Tattersalls Hotel, to a business associate, or otherwise made use of the information, for the benefit of themselves and the business associate.

In its report on the investigation, made public on 30 October 2014, the ICAC found that the former UNE chancellor engaged in corrupt conduct.

This report is no longer available online. Request the report.

RailCorp and Department of Family & Community Services - allegations of public officials corruptly soliciting funds (Operation Spector)

The ICAC investigated allegations that a former RailCorp general manager maintenance contracts, and their sister, an employee at Housing NSW, used their positions as public officials to corruptly solicit funds from other people including public officials and government contractors.

In its report on the investigation, made public on 13 October 2014, the ICAC found that both the above individuals and  four others engaged in corrupt conduct.

The ICAC stated its opinion that the advice of the Director of Public Prosecutions should be obtained with respect to the prosecution of five of the above individuals, including the former RailCorp general manager and their sibling, for offences under the Crimes Act 1900.

The ICAC also stated its opinion that consideration should be given to the taking of action against the Housing NSW employee for breaches of the Housing NSW code of conduct with a view to terminating their services with that authority.

This report is no longer available online. Request the report.

Sydney Local Health District – allegations concerning consultants engaged at the Yaralla Estate (Operation Yaralla)

This investigation came about as a result of a resolution passed by both Houses of Parliament to refer certain matters to the NSW ICAC. Section 73 of the Independent Commission Against Corruption Act 1988 provides that it is the duty of the Commission to fully investigate a matter so referred.
The ICAC investigation related to two companies with which the Sydney Local Health District (SLHD) had commercial dealings relating to Yaralla Estate matters.
With regard to the first company, the referral made to the Commission noted concerns expressed about relationships (although no specific persons were named) between that company and certain members of the Liberal Party.
With regard to the second company, the referral noted concerns relating to the payment of funds made by SLHD to the company for what was described as “limited communication advice” and relating to the company’s relationships with certain members of the Liberal Party. No specific persons were named in the referral.
The Commission’s investigation did not disclose any evidence of corrupt conduct and there were no corruption prevention issues identified in the Commission’s investigation. The report in this matter was released on 13 October 2014.
This report is no longer available online. Request the report.

Ryde City Council – allegations concerning the City of Ryde mayor (Operation Cavill)

The ICAC investigated a number of allegations involving the former mayor of the City of Ryde, and others, including the alleged release of confidential council information by the mayor on many occasions for various reasons, including in an attempt to undermine council employees, such as the former general manager.
In its report on the investigation, made public on 30 June 2014, the Commission made corrupt conduct findings against the former mayor and two others. The Commission stated its opinion that consideration should be given to obtaining the advice of the Director of Public Prosecutions (DPP) with respect to the prosecution of the above plus two additional individuals for various offences.
The ICAC stated its opinion that consideration should be given to obtaining the advice of the DPP also with respect to the prosecution of the former mayor and three then-councillors and a former councillor for offences under the Election Funding, Expenditure and Disclosures Act 1981 in relation to advertising published in The Weekly Times in August and September 2012. The Commission also recommended that the Office of Local Government give consideration to disciplinary action against the former mayor, with a view to their dismissal.
This report is no longer available online. Request the report.
NSW State Emergency Service - allegations concerning SES commissioner (Operation Dewar)
The ICAC investigated allegations that the NSW State Emergency Service (SES) commissioner took detrimental action against a deputy commissioner (“DC 1”), including dismissal from their position on 14 May 2013, in reprisal for DC 1 making allegations to the commissioner that another SES deputy commissioner (“DC 2”) had engaged in corrupt conduct.
The ICAC also examined allegations that the Commissioner improperly showed favour to DC 2 by failing to appropriately investigate allegations made by DC 1 that DC 2 had engaged in corruption. It was also alleged that in relation to the above allegations, the Commissioner made false statements or attempted to mislead an officer of the ICAC in their exercise of their functions under the Independent Commission Against Corruption Act 1988 .
In its report on the investigation, made public on 28 May 2014, the Commission made corrupt conduct findings against the commissioner. The Commission stated its opinion that the advice of the Director of Public Prosecutions should be sought with respect to the prosecution of the commissioner for an offence under the Public Interest Disclosures Act 199 4 of taking detrimental action in reprisal for a person making a public interest disclosure.
Roads and Maritime Services - allegations concerning conduct of heavy vehicle assessments (Operation Nickel)

The ICAC investigated allegations that a former heavy vehicle competency-based assessor acting on behalf of Roads and Maritime Services (RMS) solicited benefits from applicants for heavy vehicle licences, and conducted fraudulent heavy vehicle assessments. It was also alleged that the assessor signed log books certifying applicants as competent to drive a heavy vehicle, without the applicants completing the necessary assessments, in exchange for cash payments.

This report is no longer available online. Request the report.
